To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human grasping and manipulation motions can be reproduced by the Shadow Hand using 2-6 synergies, and that the iCub hand can be driven using 2-5 synergies.

1) the human grasp synergies are useful also to control a dextrous robot hand and 2) they allow to reduce the number of degrees of freedom to be controlled by the robot hand actuators, thus making the hand more dexterous and easier to control.

(i) humans automatically compensate for glove calibration errors when teleoperating a robot hand, and (ii) the resulting human-like motions of dextrous robot hand can be represented by a few synergies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of human-like synergies for dextrous robot grasping and in-hand manipulation.
a fundamental question: what is the minimal number of actuators needed in order to generate human-like precision grasps?
the analysis of human hand postures and the generation of hand synergies for dextrous robotic hands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human hand is a very effective tool for manipulating objects in daily activities and that the human hand has a very low number of effective DOFs to do that.
the human hand has a very low-dimensional control space, and the hand is able to generate a large number of grasp configurations from a very limited number of postures.
the human hand, in its ability to perform precision grasping, is not a highly redundant system, as it is often assumed, but a highly synergistic system, as we show here for the first time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human brain has a limited number of grasp synergies that can be used to control a large number of possible hand postures and motions.
human precision grasp synergies are useful for the design of robotic hands, and that the iCub hand is an appropriate platform for the development of dexterous manipulation skills.
human hand postural synergic control is not limited to power grasps, but is also present in dexterous grasping, in-hand manipulation and precision grasps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same number of synergies are enough to reproduce human precision grasps on different objects, regardless of the hand kinematics.
the same synergies are useful for different hands and that these are useful for the generation of realistic hand postures for dexterous manipulation tasks.

the synergies can be used to generate a set of hand postures for the different grasp types, which can be used to drive the hand actuators in a closed-loop fashion, to reproduce the recorded human-like hand motions.
